Introduction and meaning
Defines cruelty for s. 85: wilful conduct likely to drive the woman to suicide or cause grave injury, or harassment to coerce dowry. Charge 85, define with 86. BNS restatement of IPC 498A Expl.. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 86 is the rule on “Cruelty defined”. The section provides that for the purposes of section 85, “cruelty” means—. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 86 exists so that “Cruelty defined” has a closed legal test in Chapter V — Of Offences Against Woman and Child. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Sexual offences, assault, marriage, miscarriage, and offences against the child — placed first among the offence chapters.

The provision in detail
86. For the purposes of section 85, “cruelty” means—

(a) any wilful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) of the woman; or

(b) harassment of the woman where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to meet such demand

Definitions and key terms
“cruelty” — — (a) any wilful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) of the woman.

Essential ingredients

2. (a) any wilful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) of the woman; or

examples.title: Example 1 — simple (teaching example)
examples.body: A short everyday fact pattern is tested against “Cruelty defined”. Name BNS s. 86, list the ingredients, and say which facts match. This is a teaching example — the statute does not print a numbered illustration under this heading.

hypotheticals.question: Whether BNS s. 86 (Cruelty defined) applies, and how structured written arguments should be framed.
hypotheticals.analysis:
Step 1 — Identify the provision. The correct current-law cite is BNS s. 86 (Cruelty defined), Chapter V — Of Offences Against Woman and Child.
Step 2 — State the legal test in your own words, then list the ingredients:
   (1) For the purposes of section 85, “cruelty” means—
   (2) (a) any wilful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) of the woman; or
   (3) (b) harassment of the woman where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to meet such demand
Step 3 — Check limitations, provisos and the rest of the Chapter so you do not apply s. 86 in a vacuum.
Step 4 — Map each fact to an ingredient. Write “this fact proves ingredient (a)” or “this fact is missing, so the section is not made out”.
Step 5 — Conclude. If every essential ingredient is proved and no exception covers the case, BNS s. 86 applies. If any essential ingredient fails, say so and stop. Do not invent a different section to save the answer.

Comprehensive Written Submissions. Deepen the doctrinal synthesis with four foundational layers.

Layer 1 — Place the section in the Chapter. Sexual offences, assault, marriage, miscarriage, and offences against the child — placed first among the offence chapters.. Show why this heading sits where it sits.

Layer 2 — Work a second, slightly harder hypothetical. Change one ingredient and show why the section then fails.

learningObjectives: Master the twin limbs of statutory cruelty under BNS s. 86 (clauses a and b).
Analyze limb (a): wilful conduct driving a woman to suicide or causing grave injury/danger to life, limb, or mental/physical health.
Analyze limb (b): harassment to coerce the woman or her relatives to meet unlawful property/dowry demands.
Appreciate the structural innovation in BNS 2023 of elevating the definition of cruelty into an independent substantive section.
enhancement.definition: BNS s. 86 defines 'cruelty' for the purposes of Section 85 as: (a) any wilful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) of the woman; or (b) harassment of the woman where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to meet such demand.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Cruelty encompasses both severe wilful endangerment of physical or mental health/life and coercive dowry-related harassment, established as a definitive statutory standard.
statutoryFramework: Chapter V — Of Offences against Women and Children, BNS s. 86 (corresponding to the Explanation to IPC s. 498A).
Clause (a): Wilful conduct likely to drive woman to suicide or cause grave injury/danger to life, limb, or physical/mental health.
Clause (b): Harassment with a view to coercing her or relatives to meet unlawful demand for property/valuable security, or on account of failure to meet it.
Structural reform: Enacted as a standalone section rather than a mere explanatory footnote.
essentialIngredients: The conduct falls under Clause (a): wilful conduct likely to drive the woman to suicide or cause grave injury/danger to life, limb, or health (mental or physical); OR
The conduct falls under Clause (b): harassment of the woman with intent to coerce an unlawful demand for property or valuable security, or retaliation for failure to meet such demand.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 86 provides the legal benchmark for what constitutes 'cruelty'. By giving cruelty its own standalone section, BNS emphasizes the distinct jurisprudential identity of the concept. Clause (a) covers grave non-dowry cruelty: it requires 'wilful conduct' of such gravity that it is objectively likely to drive the woman to suicide or cause grave injury or danger to life, limb, or health (expressly recognizing mental health alongside physical health). Ordinary wear and tear of married life does not satisfy Clause (a). Clause (b) covers dowry-related cruelty: harassment designed to coerce the woman or her relatives into meeting unlawful demands for money, property, or valuable security, or punishing them for non-compliance. Either limb independently satisfies the definition.
examples: Teaching example (Clause a - Mental cruelty): An accused husband systematically isolates his wife, denies her contact with her children, subjects her to continuous humiliation regarding her appearance, and threatens to kill her, causing severe clinical depression. This wilful conduct endangers mental health under Clause (a).

Teaching example (Clause b - Coercive property demand): In-laws subject a newly married woman to continuous taunts, starvation, and physical shoving because her father refused to transfer an apartment to the husband's name. This satisfies Clause (b).
distinctions: Clause (a) Cruelty vs Clause (b) Cruelty: Clause (a) does not require any property or dowry demand, focusing on danger to life, limb, or health; Clause (b) is specifically tied to coercive property demands.
Section 86 Cruelty vs Section 80 Dowry Death: Section 86 defines cruelty generally for s. 85; Section 80 uses dowry cruelty as a prerequisite for deemed causation of death within seven years.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether continuous demands for cash accompanied by insults and locking the woman out of the matrimonial home constitute cruelty under s. 86.
Rule: Harassment aimed at coercing an unlawful demand for property or valuable security squarely falls under BNS s. 86(b).
Application: The husband's conduct was coercive, persistent, and directly linked to demands for financial assets.
Conclusion: The conduct satisfies the statutory definition of cruelty under s. 86.

shortAnswer: State BNS s. 86 definition and its role as definition section for s. 85.
List Clause (a) (grave conduct endangering life/health/suicide) and Clause (b) (unlawful property harassment).
Note express inclusion of mental health.

Detailed analysis of Clause (a): wilful conduct and threshold of gravity.
Detailed analysis of Clause (b): coercive demands for property.
Recognition of mental health in modern penal jurisprudence.
sixteenMark: Comprehensive statutory analysis of BNS s. 86 as an independent provision.
Detailed comparative dissection of Clause (a) vs Clause (b).
Threshold of mental cruelty: distinguishing domestic friction from criminal cruelty.
Judicial standards regarding proof of dowry-related harassment under Clause (b).
Application to problem scenarios and summary.

keyTakeaways: Defines cruelty for Section 85 under two independent clauses.
Clause (a) covers conduct endangering life, limb, physical or mental health, or driving to suicide.
Clause (b) covers coercive harassment for property or dowry.
Expressly recognizes mental health alongside physical health.
